drug_class: Central Nervous System Depressant / GHB derivative (Schedule III controlled substance)
purpose: Sodium oxybate is used to treat two main symptoms of narcolepsy: sudden muscle weakness triggered by emotions (called cataplexy) and excessive daytime sleepiness. It helps people with narcolepsy feel more alert during the day and have better control over their muscles. This medicine is only prescribed through a special restricted program because of its potential for misuse.
how_it_works: Sodium oxybate works by acting on certain chemical receptors in the brain that help regulate sleep. It helps improve the quality of nighttime sleep, which in turn reduces the urge to fall asleep suddenly during the day. By improving deep sleep at night, it also helps reduce episodes of sudden muscle weakness during waking hours.
common_side_effects: Nausea, dizziness, headache, bedwetting (urinating in bed at night), sleepwalking, feeling confused or groggy when waking up, vomiting, and feeling anxious. Some people also notice tremors or sweating.
warnings: This medication can cause serious breathing problems, especially if mixed with alcohol, sleep aids, or opioid pain medicines — this combination can be life-threatening. Because it works very quickly, you must only take it right before lying down in bed. Never drive or operate machinery after taking it. It is a controlled substance with risk of abuse and dependence. It is only available through a special restricted pharmacy program called the REMS program. Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, especially those that cause drowsiness.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 4.5 grams per night, split into two equal doses — one taken right at bedtime and the second taken 2.5 to 4 hours later. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose based on how well it works and how you tolerate it, up to a maximum of 9 grams per night. Each dose must be mixed with water before taking, and you should remain in bed after each dose.
